question: On previously unused human-written music captions, does the prevalence reference accept reassigned genre tags while the exact tied-score random-label reference withholds acceptance?

source.caption_filter: is_valid_subset exactly True; retain the lexicographically smallest caption_id for each track_id; join by canonical track ID
source.labels: the existing MTG uploader genre_list for each joined track; human-consensus labels are not used in this test
source.population_boundary: New Song Describer caption text on overlapping MTG tracks and uploader labels; this is not an untouched collection of recordings or independently collected genre labels.

protocol.label_selection: training fold only; frequency descending with alphabetical tie breaks
protocol.scorer: the existing deterministic bag-of-tokens log-odds scorer
protocol.control_operation: the existing two separate seeded complete-label-set rotations within training and held-out splits
protocol.metric: macro grouped-tie average precision over selected labels with held-out positives
references: exact random-label expected AP conditioned on each fitted score's tie groups
protocol.decision: lower endpoint of the descriptive paired ten-fold Student-t 95% summary for scorer minus reference above zero
protocol.primary_report: Show original and both controls against both references, including all fold values, support, confidence endpoints, and non-acceptances; do not change label count or threshold after seeing scores.
protocol.infeasibility: If a fold lacks five training-supported labels or positive held-out support, report infeasibility without retuning.

interpretation: A prospective application of a post-audit diagnostic to a new caption source, with shared MTG tracks and tags. It cannot establish operational validity on a fully untouched music collection, audio quality, or listener preference.
